fields.name: Proxy
fields.evidence: Creator bg3.exe+0x2E3DBB0 defaults it to the null handle and then stores its own param_2 = the entity the component is being added to; the only caller bg3.exe+0x2E3C320 passes local_128, a handle it has just created (FUN_14401aff0). So it is the proxy entity's own handle. Probe: 8 distinct consecutive handles 0x39DA..0x39E1 (freshly created entities).

fields.name: Source
fields.evidence: Defaults to null in bg3.exe+0x2E3DBB0; bg3.exe+0x2E3C320 then does '*(proxy + 8) = *plVar24', where plVar24 walks the entities the system is processing - the real sound entity, whose data (FixedStrings at +0x48/+0x4C/+0x50 and more of a record fetched for it) is copied onto the proxy entity's own sound-state component right after. Probe: live entity handles 0x782..0x2A01.

fields.name: UserID
fields.evidence: 4 bytes. bg3.exe+0x2E3DBB0 writes 0 and then the global default DAT_14617ceac (a constant used all over the game as the initial value of a 32-bit id); bg3.exe+0x2E3C320 then does '*(uint *)(proxy + 0x10) = *puVar22', where puVar22 walks a per-entity array of uint32 that are also used as hash keys (value % bucketCount) into a map with 0xC-byte values - one proxy is created per (source entity, id). Probe: always 0x00010001 = 65537, which is the user id of the host player in single player; the sibling component is named esv::sound::DistantSoundStateUserMapComponent.

fields.name: _Pad14
fields.evidence: Never written by the creator or by bg3.exe+0x2E3C320; probe shows 4 different garbage values (0x7FF4.., 0xFFFFFFFF). Tail padding to 8-byte alignment.

open_questions: Field names are mine (no Toolkit accessors). Layout is high confidence; meanings: self handle and source entity are read straight from the code, 'UserID' rests on the live value 65537 plus the UserMap sibling's name - the uint32 array it is copied from was not traced to its component.
Why the component stores its own entity handle at +0 was not investigated.
